summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican printed Jim Coyne's challenge to Ben Hogan, who had come to St. Louis saying he would fight Tom Allen, to fight four weeks after the Allen-Gallagher fight, with $100 posted at Allen's Fifth street saloon.

metadata.notes: The masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, August 7, 1869.'

facts.fact: Ben Hogan arrived in St. Louis saying he had come to fight Allen
Jim Coyne challenged Ben Hogan to fight four weeks after the Allen-Gallagher fight for $500 or $1,000 a side, with $100 deposited at the Wash Home or at Allen's saloon
places: Tom Allen's saloon, Fifth street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen kept a saloon on Fifth street in St. Louis in August 1869
places: Tom Allen's saloon, Fifth street, St. Louis

notes: Coyne adds that he and Allen would be happy to see their friends at Allen's saloon on Fifth street that evening. Hogan is called 'the Dutchman'.
